questions.stem: The graph of $y = f(x) + 3$ is the graph of $y = f(x)$:

options.text: Stretched by a factor of $3$ vertically

questions.explanation: Adding a constant outside the function, $f(x) + k$, translates the graph $k$ units vertically. Here $+3$ shifts the graph up by $3$.

questions.stem: The graph of $y = f(x - 2)$ is the graph of $y = f(x)$:
questions.explanation: Replacing $x$ with $(x - a)$ translates the graph $a$ units to the right. So $f(x - 2)$ shifts the graph $2$ units right.

questions.stem: The graph of $y = -f(x)$ is the graph of $y = f(x)$:
questions.explanation: Multiplying the entire function by $-1$ reflects every point in the $x$-axis: each $y$-value becomes its negative.
